project_summary: Add a brownfield “Go to offset” navigation feature to the existing hex editor UI. Users can type a decimal offset (e.g., 419) or hexadecimal with 0x prefix (e.g., 0x1A3) and jump to that byte. The editor will focus/select the byte, highlight it in both hex and ASCII columns using the existing highlight/selection mechanism, and scroll the views so the target is visible. Invalid/out-of-range offsets will show a clear error message without disrupting existing search/layout behavior.
notes: Implement minimal UI addition: a small “Go to offset” control (label + entry + button) placed near existing controls (e.g., search bar area) without changing overall layout.
Parsing rules: accept decimal (digits only) and hex with 0x/0X prefix; optionally accept plain hex without prefix only if it can be disambiguated safely (but minimum is decimal + 0x).
Validation: offset must be an integer in [0, file_size-1]; if no file is loaded, show an error message.

On success: move caret/focus to the target byte, apply highlight/selection to both hex and ASCII views (reuse existing selection/highlight tagging approach), and scroll so the byte is visible (e.g., using existing row/byte indexing math and widget yview/see calls).
On failure: display a clear error message (prefer existing status/error label mechanism; otherwise use a messagebox or dedicated inline label near the control).
Nice-to-have: bind Enter/Return in the offset entry to trigger the same jump action as the button.
Keep existing search behavior intact; do not remove/alter current search highlights unless necessary—prefer layering go-to highlight as the same selection highlight used for the active byte.
